newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PRINTING WORKERS SEE BENEFITS IN EMU.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PRINTING WORKERS SEE BENEFITS IN EMU.

text.p: The Finnish printing workers union said on Friday that the printing industry would benefit from Finnish membership of the third phase of European economic and monetary union (EMU) and warned against opting out.

"Striving to join EMU and also joining it in the first group would bring the necessary stability and confidence in the future," Pentti Levo, chairman of the Finnish Graphical Union, said according to the text of of a prepared speech.
"Opting out of EMU would unavoidably cause the kind of uncertainty that would weaken the investment climate in Finland," Levo said.

"This would further reflect on the operations of the printing industry as investment in Finland would dry up, economic activity would come to a standstill, and the advertising revenues of the printing industry would grow much thinner," Levo said.
Opting out of EMU could lead to speculation against the markka which would need to be defended at the cost of high interest rates, Levo said.
"The printing industry is in such a sensitive transition phase, that it would not survive such a situation without a wave of bankruptcies," he warned.
Turning to the autumn round of collective wage talks, Levo called for a two-year centralised wage deal built on the same objectives as the current agreement, which extends to the end of January 1998.
"In order for these objectives, low interest rates and inflation, to materialise, everyone should join the incomes agreement," Levo said.
